analysis.evidence: Pharaoh asks Abram why he said אֲחֹתִי הִוא (“She is my sister”). The words immediately following אָמַרְתָּ quote Abram’s statement.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, second person masculine singular. The ending ־תָּ marks the subject “you.”

analysis.evidence: Pharaoh quotes Abram’s words אֲחֹתִי הִוא, “She is my sister,” then calls Sarai אִשְׁתְּךָ, “your wife.” The suffix refers to Abram as the speaker of the quoted words.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state with a first-person singular possessive suffix.
